headline: Highest risk is MinerU’s MCP-enabled document ingestion creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; the pair otherwise has limited direct conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a content-writing repo with no runtime surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. MinerU exposes an MCP Server and ingests local documents by default, so if Awesome-Prompt-Engineering content is copied into a document or prompt, MinerU could parse attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise pathway is indirect but plausible.
conditions: IF content from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is pasted into a document processed by MinerU
IF MinerU treats extracted text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP access for MinerU during untrusted document processing
Use a separate workspace for prompt-library content
Add a manual review step before acting on extracted instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering has no touched data classes or filesystem surfaces, so it is not a meaningful source of leakage. MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, but its profile shows no secrets handled and offline self-isolation. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound data path that would leak A’s content by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace
IF MinerU is configured to export extracted text to an external service
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Avoid placing sensitive files in MinerU inputs
Confirm MinerU runs in offline mode
Review any export or API integration before enabling it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. MinerU has write_filesystem false and modify_git_state false, with allowlisted egress only, so there is no overlapping write surface to the same directory or git state. Any conflict would require unusual external orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF MinerU is wrapped with additional tooling that adds filesystem writes
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
Avoid adding write-capable wrappers around MinerU
Document resource ownership before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-resource repository, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative examples. MinerU performs document extraction and exposes API/MCP surfaces, which makes it plausible that extracted text or prompts from A are fed into B without verification. That creates a default-path risk of propagating bad instructions or malformed content into downstream actions.
conditions: IF MinerU consumes text derived from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering as authoritative input
IF downstream automation acts on MinerU output without human verification
mitigations: Require a verification step before downstream use
Separate source documents from operational prompts
Add a checksum or provenance tag to inputs

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is an open-source content repo with no data classes touched, and MinerU’s profile shows no secrets handled, no OAuth scopes, and offline self-isolation. There is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data pathway between them, so a compliance breach is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into MinerU inputs
IF a separate deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here
mitigations: Do not process regulated data without a separate review
